questions.solution:
Given: $A = \left[\begin{cases}2 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right]$, $B = \left[\begin{cases}{B}_{1} \text{ and } {B}_{2} \text{ and } {B}_{3}\end{cases}\right]$, ${B}_{1} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1} \\ {z}_{1}\end{array}\right]$, ${B}_{2} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {z}_{2}\end{array}\right]$ and ${B}_{3} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{3} \\ {y}_{3} \\ {z}_{3}\end{array}\right]$.

$⇒ {AB}_{1} = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1} \\ {z}_{1}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{array}{ll}2{x}_{1} + 0 + {z}_{1} \\ {x}_{1} + {y}_{1} + 0 \\ {x}_{1} + 0 + {z}_{1}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ 2{x}_{1} + {z}_{1} = 1, {x}_{1} + {y}_{1} = 0, {x}_{1} + {z}_{1} = 0$

$⇒ {x}_{1} = 1, {y}_{1} = - 1, {z}_{1} = - 1$

$⇒ {AB}_{2} = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {z}_{2}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ {AB}_{2} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2{x}_{2} + {z}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} + {y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} + {z}_{2}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ 2{x}_{2} + {z}_{2} = 2, {x}_{2} + {y}_{2} = 3, {x}_{2} + {z}_{2} = 0$

$⇒ {x}_{2} = 2, {y}_{2} = 1, {z}_{2} = - 2$

$⇒ {AB}_{3} = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{3} \\ {y}_{3} \\ {z}_{3}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ {AB}_{2} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2{x}_{3} + {z}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} + {y}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} + {z}_{3}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ 2{x}_{3} + {z}_{3} = 3, {x}_{3} + {y}_{3} = 2, {x}_{3} + {z}_{3} = 1$

$⇒ {x}_{3} = 2, {y}_{3} = 0, {z}_{3} = - 1$

$⇒ B = \left[\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 2 \\ - 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ - 1 \text{ and } - 2 \text{ and } - 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \alpha = | B | = 3$

$⇒ \beta = 1$

$⇒ {α}^{3} + {β}^{3} = 27 + 1 = 28$
questions.explanation:
Given: $A = \left[\begin{cases}2 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right]$, $B = \left[\begin{cases}{B}_{1} \text{ and } {B}_{2} \text{ and } {B}_{3}\end{cases}\right]$, ${B}_{1} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1} \\ {z}_{1}\end{array}\right]$, ${B}_{2} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {z}_{2}\end{array}\right]$ and ${B}_{3} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{3} \\ {y}_{3} \\ {z}_{3}\end{array}\right]$.

$⇒ {AB}_{1} = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1} \\ {z}_{1}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{array}{ll}2{x}_{1} + 0 + {z}_{1} \\ {x}_{1} + {y}_{1} + 0 \\ {x}_{1} + 0 + {z}_{1}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ 2{x}_{1} + {z}_{1} = 1, {x}_{1} + {y}_{1} = 0, {x}_{1} + {z}_{1} = 0$

$⇒ {x}_{1} = 1, {y}_{1} = - 1, {z}_{1} = - 1$

$⇒ {AB}_{2} = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {z}_{2}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ {AB}_{2} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2{x}_{2} + {z}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} + {y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} + {z}_{2}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ 2{x}_{2} + {z}_{2} = 2, {x}_{2} + {y}_{2} = 3, {x}_{2} + {z}_{2} = 0$

$⇒ {x}_{2} = 2, {y}_{2} = 1, {z}_{2} = - 2$

$⇒ {AB}_{3} = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}_{3} \\ {y}_{3} \\ {z}_{3}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ {AB}_{2} = \left[\begin{array}{ll}2{x}_{3} + {z}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} + {y}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} + {z}_{3}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ 2{x}_{3} + {z}_{3} = 3, {x}_{3} + {y}_{3} = 2, {x}_{3} + {z}_{3} = 1$

$⇒ {x}_{3} = 2, {y}_{3} = 0, {z}_{3} = - 1$

$⇒ B = \left[\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 2 \\ - 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ - 1 \text{ and } - 2 \text{ and } - 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \alpha = | B | = 3$

$⇒ \beta = 1$

$⇒ {α}^{3} + {β}^{3} = 27 + 1 = 28$

Let the set of all $m$, for which the system of equations $A X=B$ has a negative solution (i.e., $x < 0$ and $y < 0$ ), be the interval $(a, b)$. Then $8 \int_a^b|A| d m$ is equal to_________
questions.question: Consider the matrices : $A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}2 & -5 \\ 3 & m\end{array}\right], B=\left[\begin{array}{l}20 \\ m\end{array}\right]$ and $X=\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]$. Let the set of all $m$, for which the system of equations $A X=B$ has a negative solution (i.e., $x < 0$ and $y < 0$ ), be the interval $(a, b)$. Then $8 \int_a^b|A| d m$ is equal to_________
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & A=\left(\begin{array}{cc}2 & -5 \\ 3 & m\end{array}\right), B=\left(\begin{array}{c}20 \\ m\end{array}\right) \\ & X=\left(\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right) \\ & 2 x-5 y=20 \ldots(1)\\ & 3 x+m y=m \ldots(2)\\ & \Rightarrow y=\frac{2 m-60}{2 m+15} \\ & y < 0 \Rightarrow m \in\left(\frac{-15}{2}, 30\right)\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}=\frac{25 \mathrm{~m}}{2 \mathrm{~m}+15} \\ & \mathrm{x} < 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \in\left(\frac{-15}{2}, 0\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \in\left(\frac{-15}{2}, 0\right) \\ & |\mathrm{A}|=2 \mathrm{~m}+15 \end{aligned}$
Now, $\begin{aligned} & 8 \int_{\frac{-15}{2}}^0(2 \mathrm{~m}+15) \mathrm{dm}=8\left\{\mathrm{~m}^2+15 \mathrm{~m}\right\}_{\frac{-15}{2}}^0 \\ & \Rightarrow 8\left\{-\left(\frac{225}{4}-\frac{225}{2}\right)\right\} \\ & =8 \times \frac{225}{4}=450 \end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\left(\begin{cases}\alpha \text{ and } \beta \text{ and } \gamma\end{cases}\right)\left(\begin{cases}2 \text{ and } 10 \text{ and } 8 \\ 9 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 8 \\ 8 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } 8\end{cases}\right) = \left(\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\begin{cases}2\alpha + 9\beta + 8\gamma \text{ and } 10\alpha + 3\beta + 4\gamma \text{ and } 8\alpha + 8\beta + 8\gamma\end{cases}\right) = \left(\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right)$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$2\alpha + 2\beta + 8\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

$10\alpha + 3\beta + 4\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$8\alpha + 8\beta + 8\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(3\right)$

Now from $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(3\right)$ by cross multiplication we get,

$\dfrac{α}{1} = \dfrac{β}{6} = \dfrac{γ}{- 7} = k ⇒ \alpha = k, \beta = 6k, \gamma = - 7k$

Point $P\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ lie on the plane $2x + 4y + 3z = 5 ⇒ 2\alpha + 4\beta + 3\gamma = 5$

$⇒ 2k + 24k - 21k = 5$

$⇒ k = 1$

Hence, $6\alpha + 9\beta + 7\gamma = 6k + 54k - 49k = 11k = 11$.

Given,

$\left(\begin{cases}\alpha \text{ and } \beta \text{ and } \gamma\end{cases}\right)\left(\begin{cases}2 \text{ and } 10 \text{ and } 8 \\ 9 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 8 \\ 8 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } 8\end{cases}\right) = \left(\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\begin{cases}2\alpha + 9\beta + 8\gamma \text{ and } 10\alpha + 3\beta + 4\gamma \text{ and } 8\alpha + 8\beta + 8\gamma\end{cases}\right) = \left(\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right)$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$2\alpha + 2\beta + 8\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

$10\alpha + 3\beta + 4\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$8\alpha + 8\beta + 8\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(3\right)$

Now from $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(3\right)$ by cross multiplication we get,

$\dfrac{α}{1} = \dfrac{β}{6} = \dfrac{γ}{- 7} = k ⇒ \alpha = k, \beta = 6k, \gamma = - 7k$

Point $P\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ lie on the plane $2x + 4y + 3z = 5 ⇒ 2\alpha + 4\beta + 3\gamma = 5$

$⇒ 2k + 24k - 21k = 5$

$⇒ k = 1$

Hence, $6\alpha + 9\beta + 7\gamma = 6k + 54k - 49k = 11k = 11$.

questions.q: Let $A$ be a $2 \times 2$ matrix with $\operatorname{det}(A)=-1$ and $\operatorname{det}((A+I)(\operatorname{Adj}(A)+I))=4$. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of $A$ can be:
questions.question: Let $A$ be a $2 \times 2$ matrix with $\operatorname{det}(A)=-1$ and $\operatorname{det}((A+I)(\operatorname{Adj}(A)+I))=4$. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of $A$ can be:
questions.solution:
Let $A = \left[\begin{cases}a \text{ and } b \\ c \text{ and } d\end{cases}\right]$, so $adjA = \left|\begin{cases}a \text{ and } - b \\ - c \text{ and } d\end{cases}\right|$

Now given $\left|A\right| = - 1$

So, $ad - bc = - 1$

Now $\left|A + I\right|\left|adj A + I\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left|AadjA + adjA + A + I\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left|\left|A\right|I + adjA + A + I\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left|- I + adjA + A + I\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left|adjA + A\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + d \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } a + d\end{cases}\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left(a + d\right)2 = 4$

So, $a + d = 2$ or $- 2$
